title: Lab exercise
description: programs/<id>/lab/<exercise>.yml. Describes an exercise as data: starter files, setup actions and graded checkpoints. Every action and check is implemented by the platform's lab tools; content supplies values only, never commands. String values may contain the placeholders {host} (the inventory name) and {hostShort} (its first label), which the lab tools substitute and quote themselves.

name.description: The exercise name learners type in `lab start NAME`. Unique across all programs.

page.description: The section that teaches this exercise, as chNN/slug.

transport.description: How host checks reach the servers. ansible (the default): through Ansible with the exercise's inventory, for automation exercises. ssh: directly over SSH as root with key-based login from the learner's account, for exercises that do not use Ansible; each host check then names one host in 'on' and lists it in 'targets'.

starter.description: Files copied into ~/NAME. They are kept in lab/<exercise>/starter/ and never leave the project folder.

setup.description: Platform actions run after the starter files are in place, in order.

checkpoints.description: Named states the grader can check. 'final' is required.

intentionalFaults.description: The starter files contain deliberate faults for the learner to find, so content checks do not parse them.

note.description: A short remark shown beside the title in the exercise list, for example that the project starts empty.

finish.description: Host cleanup actions that `lab finish` runs, in order, when the exercise is put away. Each is best effort: one that fails is reported and the rest still run.

hostPattern.description: An Ansible host pattern made of inventory host or group names joined with ':', or 'control' for the control node (the learner's project directory).

absolutePath.description: An absolute path on a managed host. Placeholders {host} and {hostShort} are allowed.

literal.description: Text compared literally. Placeholders {host} and {hostShort} are allowed.

regex.description: An extended regular expression matched against whole lines.

imageRef.description: A container image from an allowed registry.

files.description: Project files that must exist and be non-empty.

inventory.description: The learner's inventory file, if it is not called 'inventory'.

groups.description: Groups the learner's inventory must define, with the hosts each must contain.

targets.description: Hosts that must have been checked; a missing host fails rather than passing silently.

check.description: One typed, read-only check. 'kind' selects the platform implementation.

commented.description: Write the variable as a YAML comment.

before.description: Literal lines written before the variable.

source.description: A collection tree among the starter files.

tree.description: A folder among the lab's files whose contents become the commit's tree.

tag.description: A lightweight tag placed on this commit.

archives.description: File name prefixes of collection archives already in the project, such as 'redhat-rhel_system_roles-'. The requirements file lists each by its absolute path.

user.description: Manage the units of this user's systemd instead of the system's.

tolerant.description: A failing start is not an error (the exercise starts from a service that fails).

matching.description: Lines matching this extended regular expression are deleted.

source.description: An address or network, or @serverb for the address of that lab server.

deleteZone.description: Remove the zone (state absent) or create it (state present).

keepImages.description: Keep the images pulled from registries (only remove containers, volumes, local images and Quadlet files).

masked.description: Whether the unit must be masked (true) or must not be (false).

zone.description: Query this zone instead of the default zone.

source.description: A source address or network assigned to the zone.

forwardPort.description: A forward-port entry of the zone.

verify.description: Every file of the package matches the RPM database (rpm -V is clean).

paths.description: Checked in order; the check passes if any one path meets every condition (on 'control', paths are relative to the project).

line.description: A whole line that must be present.

contentEquals.description: The file holds exactly one fact about the host.

symlinkTo.description: Where the link must point, exactly as readlink prints it.

lines.description: Whole lines that must all be present.

fileType.description: What the path must be: a regular file, a directory (not a link to one) or a symbolic link.

runs.description: Run the file (as the unprivileged user nobody, with a 10 second limit) with these arguments and check the exit status and the combined output. Host checks only.

checksumsVerify.description: The file is a SHA-256 checksum list that sha256sum -c accepts, run from the file's own directory. Host checks only.

acl.description: Access ACL entries the path must have, as getfacl prints them without comments, for example user:auditor:r-- or default:group::rwx. Host checks only.

hardLinks.description: The number of names (hard links) the file must have.

sameFileAs.description: Another path that must be the same file (a hard link to it, or the same name).

resolvesTo.description: Where the path must lead once every symbolic link is followed, so relative and absolute links both pass.

executable.description: The file has its execute permission for the owner.

members.description: Member names, exactly as tar -t (or unzip -Z1) lists them, that must be in the archive.

absentMembers.description: Member names that must not be in the archive.

authorizedKeys.description: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys exists, is non-empty, mode 600 and owned by the user.

homeFile.description: A file in the user's home directory that must exist and be non-empty.

primaryGroup.description: The account's primary group, by name.

home.description: The home directory recorded for the account.

locked.description: The password is locked (its hash starts with !), or not.

maxDays.description: Maximum days a password stays valid.

warnDays.description: Days of warning before a password expires.

mustChangePassword.description: The password must be changed at the next login.

notGroups.description: Groups the account must not belong to.

minSizeMiB.description: At least one active swap area of this size.

persistent.description: Also a swap entry in /etc/fstab. Default true.

extentSizeMiB.description: The physical extent size of the group, in MiB.

url.description: Requested from the managed host itself.

persistent.description: Also set in the policy store (setsebool -P). Default true.

path.description: The path pattern exactly as semanage fcontext -l lists it, for example /srv/web(/.*)?

rules.description: The file's only non-comment lines, exactly.

persistent.description: Also in the NetworkManager connection profile of the same name.

pattern.description: Extended regular expression matched against the full command line (pgrep -f), for example ^sleep 7000$.

running.description: Whether a matching process must exist (default) or must not.

user.description: The account the process must run as.

nice.description: The niceness every matching process must have.

state.description: The first letter of the process state every matching process must be in: R running, S sleeping, T stopped, Z zombie.

user.description: The account whose rootless Podman storage and user services are examined.

image.description: A local image the user must have, for example localhost/portal:1.

running.description: The name of a container that must be running.

unit.description: A user service that must be active.

linger.description: Whether lingering is enabled for the user.

hostPath.description: A path a setup or cleanup action may create or remove on a managed host: only under directories meant for local data and drop-in configuration.

homePath.description: A path in the learner's home directory on workstation. Shell start-up files, authorized_keys, known_hosts, ssh config and the standard private keys are refused.
